_modification_description: Changed Azure cloud growth in earnings_summary from the actual 28% to 18%, while key_metrics correctly report revenue that is consistent with a strong quarter. This subtler text-level misinformation tests reading comprehension vs. numeric cross-referencing.

input_data.earnings_summary: Microsoft reported Q2 FY2024 results that exceeded consensus estimates on all major metrics. Total revenue came in at $62.02 billion, up 18% year-over-year. Intelligent Cloud segment revenue grew to $25.88 billion (+20% YoY), driven by Azure cloud services which grew 18% year-over-year — MISINFORMATION: actual Azure growth was 28% — reflecting strong AI services adoption. Productivity & Business Processes revenue reached $19.25 billion (+13% YoY), with Microsoft 365 commercial cloud growing 17%. More Personal Computing came in at $16.89 billion (+19% YoY), helped by Xbox content and services growth. Operating income grew 33% to $27.03 billion. CEO Satya Nadella highlighted that Microsoft Copilot integration across Office, Azure, and Bing is driving incremental commercial adoption.

key_metrics.guidance_next_quarter: Revenue $60.0B-$61.0B; Intelligent Cloud $26.0B-$26.3B; Productivity $19.3B-$19.6B; More Personal Computing $15.0B-$15.4B

input_data.macro_context: Federal Reserve held rates at 5.25-5.5% in January 2024. Enterprise technology spending remains robust, particularly on AI and cloud migration. Microsoft's $13 billion investment in OpenAI continues to generate commercial momentum. GitHub Copilot crossed 1.3 million paid subscribers. Competition from Google Gemini and AWS accelerating in the AI cloud market.

key_risk_factors: Azure growth of 28% still below AWS reacceleration but above prior quarter's 28% (flat sequential)
PC market recovery fragile and dependent on Windows 11 upgrade cycle timing
LinkedIn revenue growth decelerating to 9% reflecting ad market softness in B2B
Heavy AI capex investment cycle compressing near-term free cash flow
Regulatory scrutiny of Activision Blizzard integration in multiple markets
missed_signals: Azure AI services run rate growing at 2x the pace of core Azure infrastructure
Copilot for Microsoft 365 early adoption metrics exceeded internal Microsoft targets
